comparison: Perfect alignment on histological findings (C43-C49). Both evaluations find the orthotopic tumor model data convincing. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate sample sizes and consistency with STAT3's role in epithelial identity. Peer reviewers affirm the animal model evidence is 'solid' without raising concerns.

Both address human tumor correlations (C70-C75, C84, C89). OpenEval finds the TCGA/COMPASS correlations well-supported with strong statistical significance. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, noting 'absence of correlation between animal studies and human pancreatic cancers' and suggesting more patient data would strengthen the study.

Both address therapeutic implications (C86-C88, C94). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these claims extend beyond experimental data and require drug treatment validation. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'the study would benefit from additional cause-and-effect type experiments' for these speculative claims.

Both address main conclusions (C3, C78, C79, C93). OpenEval finds these well-supported by convergent evidence from multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers unanimously affirm the main finding, with the editor noting 'convincing evidence' and Reviewer 1 calling it a 'valuable finding' with 'solid' evidence.

Both address STAT3-SMAD4 epistasis (C15-C16, C66-C69, plus C14, C37-C39, C65 in peer). OpenEval emphasizes systematic genetic controls and clear demonstration of functional antagonism. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this key finding, with Reviewer 1 highlighting the surprising phenotype reversal without challenge.

Both address transcriptomic EMT analysis (C51-C57, plus C4, C36, C58-C61 in peer). OpenEval finds comprehensive bioinformatic support for partial EMT characterization. Peer reviewers accept the RNA-seq findings without criticism, with Reviewer 3 acknowledging the mesenchymal-like phenotypes induced by KRAS and STAT3 KO.

Partial overlap on in vivo tumor suppression (C28-C31 shared, plus C27 in OpenEval and C21, C32-C33 in peer). OpenEval emphasizes dose-dependent relationships and limiting dilution data. Peer reviewers accept the mechanistic findings about STAT3 mutations affecting KRASG12D fibroblasts without challenge.

Both address KRAS dependency analysis (C62-C64, plus C58-C61 in OpenEval). OpenEval highlights strong statistical evidence and quantitative EMT/RAS dependency scores. Peer reviewers accept the correlation between STAT3 loss and KRAS-independent signature without challenge, viewing it as supporting the main model.

Both address mechanistic requirements via DBD mutants (C32-C33, plus C21, C28-C31 in peer). OpenEval finds strong evidence that transcriptional activity is required for suppressive function. Peer reviewers accept these mechanistic findings as part of the overall demonstration without raising concerns.

Partial overlap on transformation assays (C19-C20, C26 shared, plus C17-C18, C21-C25 in OpenEval and C13, C27, C92 in peer). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple approaches demonstrating STAT3 lacks intrinsic oncogenicity. Peer reviewers implicitly accept lack of growth effects as part of STAT3's non-driver characterization.

Minimal overlap on mechanistic pathways (C34-C35 shared, plus C36-C39 in OpenEval and C5 in peer). OpenEval finds RNA-seq and epistasis experiments support TGF-β mechanism. Peer reviewers accept these supporting mechanistic findings without specific criticism as part of the overall model.

Minimal overlap (C4 only). OpenEval finds the RNA-seq correlation between STAT3 and KRAS well-supported with quantification. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the transcriptional analysis without challenge.

Both address C94 regarding rare STAT3 GOF mutations. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting this is speculative despite plausible mechanism. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, suggesting additional cause-and-effect experiments would strengthen speculative claims.

Both address C84 on SMAD4 status and tumor phenotype. OpenEval finds this observation appropriately motivates investigation of additional modifiers. Peer reviewers rate the broader human correlation analysis UNCERTAIN, wanting stronger patient data.

Both address C89 on STAT3 phosphorylation levels in human samples. OpenEval finds the observation appropriately documented but notes functional implications need testing. Peer reviewers include this in their UNCERTAIN rating of human correlations, wanting more patient data.

Both address C17-C18 on genetic model methodology. OpenEval includes these in comprehensive evaluation of transformation assays. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the technical approaches as appropriate without questioning methodology.

Both address C92 on STAT3 as non-driver. OpenEval finds this well-supported by negative transformation results in non-KRAS contexts. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this characterization as part of the overall non-driver role without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates literature context claims (C1-C2, C6-C12, C40-C42, C50, C65, C76-C77, C80-C83, C91) as appropriately supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers implicitly accept the contextual framing.
